Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

ipw 1.4.0

New features

  • ipwpoint(): new estimand argument. For a binomial exposure: "ATE" (default), "ATT" (effect in the treated), "ATC" (effect in the untreated) and "ATO" (overlap weights). For family = "multinomial" and "ordinal": "ATT", with the new argument focal naming the level whose effect is targeted, and "ATO" (generalized overlap weights; Li & Li 2019). For the effect in the controls of a categorical exposure, use "ATT" with focal set to the control level.
  • New ipwvcov() (experimental): the variance-covariance matrix of the coefficients of a marginal structural model, taking the estimation of the weights into account (M-estimation with stacked estimating equations). Supported:
    • ipwpoint() weights for a binary exposure with a logistic model (any estimand), with an lm(), glm() or coxph() model (right-censored data, one row per person);
    • ipwtm() weights with family = "binomial", link = "logit" and any type, or a list of ipwtm()/ipwpoint() results whose weights multiply (e.g. treatment times censoring weights), with an lm(), glm() or counting-process coxph() model on the long data. Scores are summed within subject.
    Other cases (other families or links, truncated weights, smooth terms) give an error; use the bootstrap there. Checked against numerical derivatives of the estimating equations, WeightIt::glm_weightit() and PSweight. With heavy-tailed weights no normal-theory interval is reliable, whichever method gives the standard error (see ?ipwvcov).
  • New ipwprobtm(): time-varying weights from probabilities estimated elsewhere (for example with machine learning), multiplied over time within each subject. For a point treatment the weights are simply num / den.
  • ipwpoint(): new families for count exposures ("poisson", "negbin") and skewed continuous exposures ("gamma", "lognormal").
  • ipwtm(): type = "all" (exposures that switch back and forth) now works for family = "multinomial", "ordinal" and "survival" (recurrent exposure events, Graffeo et al. 2018).
  • Smooth terms (s(), te(), ti(), t2()) in model formulas are fitted with mgcv::gam(): in ipwpoint() for the binomial, gaussian and poisson families, and in ipwtm() for the binomial family. Without smooth terms the models are still fitted with glm().
  • ipwpoint() results carry the attributes "estimand", "exposure" and (for ATT and ATC) "focal". ipwtm() results carry the attributes "family", "type", "id" and "sort.order". The list elements and weights are unchanged.

Changes

  • Survival weights and the time grid (caution for older versions). ipwtm() with family = "survival" and type = "first" or "cens" now computes each row’s probability from the baseline hazard over that row’s own interval (tstart, timevar]. ipw 1.3.2 and earlier used the increase in the baseline hazard since the previous time point in the whole data set, which is right only when every subject’s follow-up is split at all times that occur in the data (the “full time grid”, as in the JSS paper, haartdat and Example 2 of ?ipwtm). For data on the full grid the weights are unchanged. Data with individual visit times can now be used directly; if you used such data with an older version, re-run the analysis with this version. The article “Survival weights and the time grid” shows how to check whether your data were on the full grid.
  • License changed back to GPL (>= 2), the license of ipw before 1.3.0 (1.3.0 to 1.3.2 were MIT).
  • Two functions that were only in development versions on GitHub, never on CRAN, changed: ipwprob() was renamed ipwprobtm() and now handles time-varying exposures only, and ipwboot() was removed (the bootstrap is shown in ?ipwpoint and vignette("ipw") instead).
  • Existing calls give the same weights as before (except for the time-grid change above), checked by regression tests against ipw 1.2.1.1. A covariate named s, te, ti or t2 is treated as an ordinary variable.

Bug fixes

  • ipwpoint() and ipwtm(): offset() terms in the numerator and denominator formulas were silently dropped, so the weights were wrong. This affected ipw 1.3.1 and 1.3.2; ipw 1.2.1.1 was fine.
  • ipwpoint() and ipwtm(): a binomial (or survival) 0/1 exposure stored as a factor or character is now used by its labels. With factor levels in the order c("1", "0") the probabilities of the two exposure values were swapped, giving wrong weights.
  • ipwpoint(): denominator = ~ . works again, as in ipw 1.2.1.1. In ipwtm() a . is an error, because it would include the id, time and exposure columns.
  • ipwtm(), family = "survival": ties passed through ... to coxph() was ignored (Efron was always used); it is now passed on.
  • ipwtm(): a covariate called selvar was replaced by the internal selection indicator; it is now used as the user’s covariate.
  • family = "ordinal": a character exposure is now an error, and an unordered factor whose levels are not numbers gives a warning, because the levels would be ordered alphabetically. Use an ordered factor.
  • Clearer errors instead of wrong results or obscure messages: duplicated id/timevar combinations in ipwtm(), tstart >= timevar, an exposure that takes one value, infinite values in model variables, a non-numeric gaussian exposure, den/num above 1 in ipwprobtm(), missing or non-positive weights in ipwplot(). tstartfun() warns when follow-up times are <= -1.
  • The ipwtm() examples no longer call graphics.off(), which closed all of the user’s graphics devices.

Documentation

  • New vignette, “Inverse probability weighting with ipw” (vignette("ipw")), covering every function, with sections on standard errors (bootstrap, ipwvcov()), covariate balance with cobalt and the effective sample size.
  • “Standard errors” paragraphs in ?ipwpoint and ?ipwtm: when the bootstrap helps, when robust standard errors that treat the weights as known can be too small, and which cases ipwvcov() supports.
  • New “ipw or WeightIt?” section in the README and the vignette.
  • New articles on the package website (https://tranhung93.github.io/ipw/): “Methods” (formulas and code for the new features), “Simulation study”, “Bugs fixed after ipw 1.3.2”, “Survival weights and the time grid” and “ipw, WeightIt and PSweight side by side”.

Tests

  • Weights and standard errors are compared with WeightIt and PSweight (both in Suggests), with numerical derivatives of the estimating equations, and with weights computed by hand; regression tests against ipw 1.2.1.1.

ipw 1.3.2

CRAN release: 2026-11-01

Bug fixes

  • ipwpoint(): weights.trunc was wrong whenever trunc was set. The lower and upper quantiles were recycled across rows, so every truncated weight was replaced by one of the two bounds. Weights are now clipped at the trunc and 1 - trunc quantiles, and weights between the bounds are left unchanged.
  • ipwtm() with family = "multinomial" or "ordinal": predicted probabilities are now matched to the observed exposure by level name rather than by column position. 1.3.1 stopped with an error for a two-level exposure, or when an exposure level did not occur among the rows used to fit the models.
  • ipwpoint() with family = "multinomial" now works for a two-level exposure; 1.3.1 stopped with an error (“Observed exposure levels do not match fitted probability levels”).
  • Added a test for unstabilized weights (no numerator) with family = "multinomial" and "ordinal" in ipwpoint(). These failed in 1.3.0 and were fixed by the 1.3.1 rewrite (#3, @adcascone).
  • ipwtm() with type = "first" and family = "multinomial" / "ordinal": a switch is again defined as the first record at any level other than the lowest level in the whole data set, as in ipw <= 1.2.1.1. In 1.3.1 the reference level was chosen separately for each subject.

Improvements

  • ipwtm() now checks that all model variables exist and contain no missing values, and that a binomial/survival exposure is coded 0/1, with clear error messages instead of errors from inside glm() / coxph().
  • ipwtm() with family = "survival" now stops with a clear message when a formula contains strata(), which is not supported.
  • Fitted models returned in num.mod / den.mod no longer carry an inlined copy of the data in their call, so printing them is readable again.
  • ipwpoint() and ipwtm() share one set of internal helpers for argument checks, formula construction, probability extraction and truncation.
  • Removed blanket import() of whole packages; all calls use pkg::fun. methods is no longer imported.

Tests

  • Test suite expanded: exact checks of truncation, row-order invariance, two-level multinomial vs binomial equivalence, and error messages.
  • New regression test against ipw 1.2.1.1 (reference weights created with data-raw/make-regression-fixtures.R).

ipw 1.3.1

CRAN release: 2026-10-30

  • Core Refactoring (ipwtm, ipwpoint, ipwplot, tstartfun):
    • Improved defensive input validation, parameter checking, and error messages across all core functions.
    • Modernized formula construction (as.formula()) to eliminate fragile eval(parse(text = ...)) string manipulations.
    • Fixed variable symbol evaluation issues when passing variables as function arguments rather than raw names.
    • Modularized ipwtm into dedicated family modeling engines (binomial, survival, multinomial, ordinal, gaussian).
    • Replaced manual survival hazard step-differencing with continuous baseline hazard interpolation using survival::basehaz and stats::approx.
    • Refactored tstartfun to use safe column evaluation and direct vector lag logic (c(-1, t[-length(t)])).
  • Test Suite Expansion:
    • Upgraded testthat suite to 3rd edition specs, expanding coverage for multinomial, ordinal, gaussian, unstabilized models, weight truncation, and invalid parameter rejection.

ipw 1.3.0

CRAN release: 2026-01-27

  • New maintainer: Hung Thai Tran.
  • License changed to MIT (earlier versions: GPL (>= 2)).
